status_semantics.OPEN: Not refuted, but one or more named proof, typing, source, or review obligations remain.
status_semantics.VERIFIED: The narrow statement in the record was checked directly; this is not external peer review or proof-assistant certification.
status_semantics.RETRACTED: The source statement is false as written or is withdrawn as an admissible theorem claim.

records.title: Blanket v7.3-to-v7.4 theorem inheritance
records.original_excerpt: All definitions, theorems, axioms, and proofs from previous versions remain valid and unchanged.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: Provide a signature diff and a theorem-by-theorem proof-transport audit; blanket inheritance cannot supply either.
records.corrected_statement: Version 7.4 extends the v7.3 materials. A prior theorem is inherited only after its definitions, hypotheses, and proof have an explicit compatible migration record.

records.title: Unresolved cross-reference placeholders
records.original_excerpt: The registered integrated text contains 84 literal '??' tokens on 71 lines.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: Resolve every placeholder to an existing numbered item, add a missing item, or remove the dependency; then require zero literal '??' tokens.
records.corrected_statement: No proof chain is citation-complete while an edge terminates at an unresolved placeholder.

records.title: Type-correct Noe-Cov-3 generator
records.original_excerpt: The corrected Noe-Cov-3 uses the counit epsilon_I:R(I)->I rather than the oppositely directed unit.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: A generator of a sieve on I must have codomain I.
records.corrected_statement: Noe-Cov-3 is type-correct when it requires epsilon_I:R(I)->I to lie in the sieve on I.

records.title: Reduction of Noetic coverage
records.original_excerpt: Noe-Cov-2 and Noe-Cov-3 each imply Noe-Cov-1 under the stated ACBE and section-retraction axioms.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: ACBE reflexivity places an identity in the descent-generated sieve, and epsilon_I has section eta_I; either condition yields a maximal sieve or a jointly-surjective singleton.
records.corrected_statement: Under the stated axioms J_noe equals jointly-surjective coverage. The ACBE and RPM clauses do not retain independent nonmaximal covering information.

records.title: Grothendieck-topology and topos structure theorem
records.original_excerpt: Theorem 26.27 makes J_noe a Grothendieck topology and Theorem 26.29 invokes general topos theory.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: Freeze a small category, verify pullback closure and every coverage axiom at that exact category, and cite the general Grothendieck-topos theorem precisely.
records.corrected_statement: If Noetica is small with the stated pullbacks and J_noe satisfies the Grothendieck axioms, then Sh(Noetica,J_noe) is a Grothendieck topos. This does not prove the TKS-specific site data.

records.title: Representable Idea object treated as a sheaf
records.original_excerpt: The Idea base type is called the representable sheaf y(I).
records.counterexample_or_obligation: Sets of size at most two with injections and jointly-surjective covers satisfy the setup but are not subcanonical; the two point inclusions do not give the required representable gluing into a singleton.
records.corrected_statement: Use the sheafification a_J(yI), or explicitly add and label subcanonicity as an axiom, or change the site and prove subcanonicity.

records.title: RPM state-and-failure monad typed over Noetica
records.original_excerpt: R(X):=AcqState->(X+Failed)xAcqState is called an endofunctor Noetica->Noetica and its bind laws are asserted.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: Specify the base category and show it has the state object, failure coproduct, exponentials, functor action on morphisms, unit, multiplication or bind, and the monad laws; also relate this R to the section-retraction R in the topos chapter.
records.corrected_statement: The displayed construction is the standard state-plus-exception monad on a suitably closed category such as Set. Its restriction to Noetica and its identity with the realization endofunctor remain unproved.

records.title: Every finite noetic map has a fixed point
records.original_excerpt: Each noetic is claimed to have at least one fixed point, citing Brouwer on a finite space.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: The transposition on a two-element set is a total finite endomap with no fixed point and a two-cycle.
records.corrected_statement: Every total endomap of a nonempty finite set has an eventually periodic orbit, but it need not have a fixed point.

records.title: Noetic Dimension Theorem for a single sequence orbit
records.original_excerpt: Symbol frequencies of one transfinite sequence are asserted to bound the box dimension of its orbit closure.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: The source itself says eventual periodicity gives dimension zero but then assigns the periodic 1-4-7 example dimension log(3)/log(10). Frequency entropy alone does not determine a single-sequence orbit-closure dimension.
records.corrected_statement: Entropy-dimension results require an explicitly defined shift space or invariant measure, metric, stationarity/ergodicity hypotheses, and a proof connecting typical-word growth to the chosen set. Treat the current quantity only as a declared diversity/entropy score.

records.title: Eventual contraction from finiteness
records.original_excerpt: A pigeonhole argument is used to claim that sufficiently long compositions from any two-map finite IFS contain a strict contraction.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: On two points take S={identity,swap}. Every composition is a permutation and has discrete-metric Lipschitz constant one.
records.corrected_statement: Eventual strict contraction requires an explicit contractive generator or a separately proved synchronizing property; finiteness alone gives neither.

records.title: Finite Hutchinson stabilization versus unique attractor
records.original_excerpt: H_S^n(I) is claimed to decrease and stabilize within 40 steps, and the result is called the attractor by uniqueness.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: Monotonicity proves the descending-chain result, but uniqueness of a nonempty fixed compact set requires contractivity or another hypothesis.
records.corrected_statement: For a finite carrier X, H_S^n(X) descends and stabilizes after at most |X| strict decreases at the greatest fixed subset reached from X. Do not call it the unique metric attractor without a uniqueness theorem.

records.title: Sequential prefix-IFS attractor intersection
records.original_excerpt: Adding noetics to prefix IFSs is said to produce a decreasing attractor chain whose intersection is the full attractor.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: On {0,1}, the IFS containing only constant-0 has attractor {0}; adding constant-1 gives attractor {0,1}. The prefix attractors expand, so their intersection is not the full attractor.
records.corrected_statement: Adding generators makes the Hutchinson operator pointwise larger. Any limit theorem must use the correct monotonic direction and define the nonautonomous/full-system attractor separately.

records.title: Finite repetition implies pointwise stabilization
records.original_excerpt: Eventual repetition on a finite carrier is used to conclude that every later value is constant after a stabilization ordinal.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: The swap map on two states yields a period-two orbit forever; repetition detects a cycle, not a constant tail.
records.corrected_statement: A deterministic orbit on a finite carrier is eventually periodic with preperiod and period each bounded by |X|. Stabilization requires period one or an additional contraction/order hypothesis.

records.title: Graph Laplacian sign, kernel, conservation, and symmetry
records.original_excerpt: For Delta=sum w_k(P_k-I), negative semidefiniteness, a common-invariant kernel, conservation, and symmetry are asserted for general deterministic noetics.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: For the constant map f(0)=f(1)=0, Delta=[[0,0],[1,-1]] on functions and x=(2,1) gives x^T Delta x=1>0. A measure-preserving permutation need not be symmetric.
records.corrected_statement: The formula defines a generally nonnormal Markov difference operator. A self-adjoint negative semidefinite Laplacian requires a specified invariant measure and reversible/symmetrized construction; common-invariant and conservation claims need separate hypotheses.

records.title: Orthogonal spectral decomposition of the graph operator
records.original_excerpt: The general graph operator is assigned real ordered eigenvalues and an orthogonal eigenbasis.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: The two-state constant-map Delta has eigenvectors for 0 and -1 that are not orthogonal under the stated Euclidean inner product.
records.corrected_statement: An orthonormal eigenbasis and real ordering follow for a self-adjoint Laplacian, not for an arbitrary deterministic transition difference. Otherwise use nonnormal spectral/Jordan or singular-value analysis.

records.title: Noetic-Laplacian invariance and mixing correspondence
records.original_excerpt: Average invariance is equated with invariance under every deterministic noetic, followed by spectral-gap mixing and a stabilization-time bound.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: On {0,1,2}, f=(0,0,2), g=(0,2,2), and h=(0,1,2) as a function vector satisfy (P_f h+P_g h)/2=h while neither P_f h nor P_g h equals h.
records.corrected_statement: The operator identity Delta=P_S-I is algebraic. Pointwise common invariance, exponential mixing, and any link to stabilization require named irreducibility, aperiodicity, reversibility/normality, norm, and comparison hypotheses.

records.title: Norm of a deterministic standard-basis lift
records.original_excerpt: The displayed theorem states ||nu_k||_op<=1 even though its own calculation obtains a maximum-fiber multiplicity bound.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: The constant map on two states has lift A=[[1,1],[0,0]] and ||A||=sqrt(2).
records.corrected_statement: For f:X->Y and A_f e_x=e_{f(x)}, ||A_f||=sqrt(max_y |f^{-1}(y)|). In particular the lift is a contraction exactly when f is injective on a nonempty finite domain.

records.title: Idempotent deterministic lift is a projector
records.original_excerpt: Classical idempotence is cited as a projector property for the Hilbert-space lift.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: The two-state constant lift satisfies A^2=A but A is not self-adjoint and A* A is not a projection, so A is neither an orthogonal projector nor a partial isometry.
records.corrected_statement: An idempotent linear operator is an oblique projection in the algebraic sense. It is an orthogonal projector only when self-adjoint; partial-isometry status requires A* A to be an orthogonal projection.

records.title: Occupation trace and image-support identities
records.original_excerpt: O_k=nu_k*nu_k is said to measure image support, be a projector for an idempotent noetic, and satisfy Tr(O_k)=rank(nu_k)=|Im(nu_k)|.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: The definition indexes a noetic by 1,...,22 although the registered ontology has ten noetics. For the two-state constant lift, Tr(A* A)=2 while rank(A)=|Im(f)|=1, and A* A records input-fiber collisions.
records.corrected_statement: First type k in the frozen noetic index set. For a deterministic lift A_f, Tr(A_f* A_f)=|X|. A_f* A_f is the input-collision Gram matrix. Output support lies on A_f A_f* and must be normalized fiberwise to obtain the orthogonal projector onto span{e_y:y in Im(f)}.

records.title: Spectral and contraction properties of quantum fractal products
records.original_excerpt: Products of idempotent lifts are asserted to have spectrum in {0,1} and norm at most one.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: A single two-state constant lift is already idempotent with norm sqrt(2), refuting the norm clause. Products of noncommuting idempotents need not be idempotent or have only 0/1 spectrum.
records.corrected_statement: A fixed-point basis vector gives eigenvalue one when it exists. Norm and spectral claims for products require contraction and normality/commutation hypotheses stated operator by operator.

records.title: Canonical fractal normal forms
records.original_excerpt: Arbitrary words are said to reduce recursively to an irreducible normal-form subsequence.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: Define typed rewrite rules and prove termination and confluence, or define a fixed-order shortlex representative and re-normalize after composition.
records.corrected_statement: The displayed rows are proposed rewrite conventions, not a unique-normal-form theorem, until typing, termination, confluence, and composition compatibility are proved.

records.title: Alternating dual pairs converge by cancellation
records.original_excerpt: An alternating dual sequence is described as collapsing to the identity limit.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: If b=a^{-1} and a is nonidentity, partial products alternate between a and identity, giving period two rather than convergence.
records.corrected_statement: Adjacent inverse pairs may be reduced in finite words under a proved equality. Infinite alternating partial products need a topology and convergence hypothesis; algebraic cancellation alone gives a two-cycle.

records.title: Numerical spectral-radius classification table
records.original_excerpt: The table assigns radius 0, <1, 1, or >1 to noetics without supplying their finite maps or matrices.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: Every standard-basis lift of a total endomap on a nonempty finite set has spectral radius exactly one because every functional graph contains a cycle. The identity lift in particular has radius one, not zero.
records.corrected_statement: Remove all numerical radius/eigenclass entries until each noetic has a versioned concrete map or matrix. Under the stated total deterministic lift, the spectral radius is one for every noetic.

records.title: Noetic quasi-category and mapping-space construction
records.original_excerpt: N_infinity is declared a quasi-category, inner horn fillers are identified with fractal interpolation, and its mapping spaces are called Kan complexes.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: Specify every simplicial degree and face/degeneracy map, prove the simplicial identities and inner horn fillers, and use a standard mapping-space construction before invoking Kan fibrancy.
records.corrected_statement: This is a programmatic proposal for a noetic quasi-category, not an established construction or theorem.

records.title: Continuous target for differential noetic geometry
records.original_excerpt: The corrected chapter embeds the 40 Ideas as simplex vertices and sends a smooth manifold into the open 39-simplex.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: A finite discrete Idea set has zero-dimensional tangent spaces; the open simplex supplies a valid smooth target while preserving vertices only in the closed boundary.
records.corrected_statement: A noetic manifold is a smooth M with a smooth state map sigma:M->int(Delta^39); the discrete Ideas embed as boundary vertices of the closed simplex and are not themselves the smooth target.

records.title: Noetic dimension as a declared score
records.original_excerpt: dim_sigma(p)=dim(T_p M)+rank(d sigma_p) is named noetic dimension.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: The sum may be defined, but it is not the manifold dimension, graph dimension, image dimension, or a standard invariant without an invariance theorem.
records.corrected_statement: Define ndscore_sigma(p):=dim(M)+rank(d sigma_p) as the noetic dimension score. Any invariance or empirical interpretation requires a separate theorem.

records.title: Lingering claim that the finite Idea space is a natural manifold
records.original_excerpt: The later synthesis chapter says the Idea space I carries a natural noetic manifold structure with coordinates, connection, geodesics, exp, and log.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: This contradicts the corrected chapter's explicit statement that the discrete 40-point I is not the smooth target. No atlas, metric, connection, exponential, or logarithm is constructed here.
records.corrected_statement: Replace I by a named smooth model such as int(Delta^39), and define its metric/connection before using geodesics, exp, or log; otherwise retain I only as a discrete vertex set.

records.title: Approximate dual cancellation
records.original_excerpt: Composition of dual pairs is said to approximately yield the identity, with no metric, tolerance, or concrete maps.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: Supply concrete same-carrier maps and a named norm/metric with an error bound; surrounding composition can amplify local error by operator norms.
records.corrected_statement: Call the paired arrow a reverse or dual unless a true inverse law is proved. An approximate cancellation theorem must state composition order, carrier, norm, local error, and amplification factors.

records.title: Kleene fixed-point specialization
records.original_excerpt: Kleene convergence is stated for a Scott-continuous noetic fractal and a noetic dcpo asserted elsewhere.
records.counterexample_or_obligation: Construct the dcpo with bottom, prove directed completeness and Scott continuity of the exact endomap, and distinguish this order limit from metric or finite-state convergence.
records.corrected_statement: For a pointed dcpo D and Scott-continuous Phi:D->D, lfp(Phi)=sup_n Phi^n(bottom). Applying this standard theorem to TKS remains conditional on a verified D and Phi.
